newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA SAYS CHINA HAS SENT MISSILES TO PAKISTAN.
newsitem.headline: INDIA SAYS CHINA HAS SENT MISSILES TO PAKISTAN.

text.p: India on Thursday accused China of supplying ballistic missiles to Pakistan and helping its arch-foe build a missile factory.

"Government are aware of supply of M-11 ballistic missiles by China to Pakistan, as well as Chinese assistance to build a factory to manufacture ballistic missiles at Fatehjung, near Rawalpindi," junior Foreign Minister Kamala Sinha said.

Her written answer to a question by a member of the upper house of parliament, released on Thursday, was believed to be first time India had publicly and unambiguously accused China of supplying M-11 missiles to Pakistan.

The U.S. Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) concluded last year that China had delivered to Pakistan 30 ready-to-launch M-11 missiles, each capable of carrying a 1,100-lb (500-kg) warhead more than 185 miles (300 miles).
Last month Time magazine said the CIA had located a facility at Rawalpindi, near Pakistan's capital Islamabad, that could make Chinese M-11 missiles.

Both Pakistan and China denied the report, and Islamabad dismissed fears voiced in the United States and India about its alleged missile development, saying it was doing nothing contrary to its commitments.

India has been reluctant to accuse China directly of supplying ballistic missiles to Pakistan. In July, India referred to "outside assistance" to Pakistan's missile programme, without directly accusing China.
On Tuesday, India and China pledged to look to the 21st century in a cooperative spirit as they ended a fresh round of talks towards settling a stubborn border dispute which led to war in 1962.

In a separate statement in response to another legislator's question released on Thursday, the government said it was aware of "reports regarding defence cooperation between China and Pakistan and supply of military equipment and technology by China to Pakistan".
It said the acquisition of weapons by Pakistan "beyond its legitimate requirements poses a threat to India's security and is not conducive to peace and stability in the region".
But it said China had indicated its military exports to Pakistan "are part of normal state-to-state cooperation, that they are limited and that they do not affect the balance of power in the region".
It said China "has also said that it does not support or assist other countries in developing nuclear weapons".
Last year, the Washington Times newspaper said China had sold nuclear weapons-related equipment to Pakistan. Both Beijing and Islamabad denied the report, which was based on a CIA memorandum.
Sinha said in response to a third parliamentarian's question that New Delhi was "aware of Pakistan's clandestine nuclear weapons programme", and that India would safeguard its interests.
India exploded an atomic device in 1974 but says it has not built a nuclear weapon.
